$comment: Every source here was opened and read on 2026-11-09 (abstract page, HTML or PDF). 'verified' lists what was checked against the source itself. 'cautions' records inconsistencies found inside the source or between the source and the paper outline.

sources.title: Comparing AI Coding Agents: A Task-Stratified Analysis of Pull Request Acceptance
sources.venue: MSR 2026 (23rd Int. Conf. on Mining Software Repositories)
sources.role: Closest prior work. Task-stratified PR acceptance of five agents on 7,156 AIDev PRs.
cautions: The 29 pp gap is chore 84.0% vs perf 55.4% in v1 (exactly 28.6 pp). v2 (7 May 2026) headlines a 16 pp gap, docs 82.1% vs features 66.1%. Name the version when quoting.
The abstract says Cursor leads fix tasks (80.4%), but Section 4.3 reports Codex at 83.0% on fix.

sources.title: How Do AI Coding Agents Contribute to Software Development? An Empirical Study of Agentic Pull Requests
sources.venue: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst. 37(4), Article 111
sources.role: Agentic vs human PRs across lifecycle stages (quarters) in 489 Python repositories.
cautions: Table 1 column labels look inconsistent with Table 3; use the GLMM estimates from RQ1 only.

sources.title: A Task-Level Evaluation of AI Agents in Open-Source Projects
sources.role: Acceptance, review-discussion volume and commit-message quality by agent and task type (AIDev-pop, 33,549 PRs).
cautions: The RQ2 text calls Copilot and Devin 'closest' in comment volume, which the reported averages do not support.

sources.title: The Rise of AI Teammates in Software Engineering (SE) 3.0: How Autonomous Coding Agents Are Reshaping Software Engineering
sources.role: First AIDev release (v1: 456,535 PRs) with agent vs human acceptance and turnaround in AIDev-pop.
cautions: The outline's 932,791 PRs / 116,211 repositories figure comes from the later MSR'26 dataset paper (li2026aidev), not from this v1.

sources.title: AIDev: Studying AI Coding Agents on GitHub
sources.role: Dataset paper: 932,791 agentic PRs, 116,211 repositories, 72,189 developers; curated 33,596-PR subset.

sources.title: Agentic AI in the Software Development Lifecycle: Architecture, Empirical Evidence, and the Reshaping of Software Engineering
sources.role: Survey with a three-tier view of productivity evidence (controlled, field, longitudinal) and a SWE-bench Verified trajectory.
cautions: Calls SWE-bench Verified a 489-task subset; OpenAI's release says 500.
The field-experiment tier cites [19], whose reference entry is a different paper (Dohmke et al.). Cite Cui et al. directly.
Tool-level scores in its Table 2 are marked approximate; do not quote them as measurements.

sources.title: Beyond Bug Fixes: An Empirical Investigation of Post-Merge Code Quality Issues in Agent-Generated Pull Requests
sources.role: SonarQube differential analysis of 1,210 merged agent bug-fix PRs.
cautions: Claude Code (15 PRs) and Cursor (40 PRs) samples are small.

sources.title: Beyond Final Code: A Process-Oriented Error Analysis of Software Development Agents in Real-World GitHub Scenarios
sources.role: Execution errors in 3,977 trajectories of 8 agents on SWE-bench Verified; three benchmark platform bugs.

sources.title: Are We All Using Agents the Same Way? An Empirical Study of Core and Peripheral Developers' Use of Coding Agents
sources.role: How core vs peripheral developers delegate, review, modify and verify 9,427 agentic PRs.

sources.title: TDAD: Test-Driven Agentic Development - Reducing Code Regressions in AI Coding Agents via Graph-Based Impact Analysis
sources.role: Code-to-test impact map cuts regressions on SWE-bench Verified; TDD prompting alone increased them.
cautions: Small samples (100 and 25 instances), quantised local models, no significance tests.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.role: Original benchmark: 2,294 issues from 12 Python repositories.

sources.title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
sources.role: 500 human-validated instances screened by 93 developers.

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
sources.role: Agent-computer interface; 12.5% pass@1 on SWE-bench.

sources.title: SWE-Bench+: Enhanced Coding Benchmark for LLMs
sources.role: Solution leakage and weak tests in SWE-bench; new 548-instance post-cutoff set.
cautions: Reports both 3.97% and 5.49% as SWE-Agent+GPT-4's filtered rate.

sources.title: AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement
sources.role: Program-structure-aware code search plus spectrum-based localisation; 19% on SWE-bench Lite at about $0.43 per issue.
cautions: Venue taken from the published version; the arXiv page lists no venue.

sources.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
sources.role: Open agent platform evaluated on 15 benchmarks including SWE-bench and WebArena.

sources.title: SWE-bench Multimodal: Do AI Systems Generalize to Visual Software Domains?
sources.role: 617 JavaScript instances with images; best system (SWE-agent) 12%.

sources.title: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents
sources.role: 50k synthetic task instances from 128 repositories; SWE-agent-LM-32B reaches 40.2% on Verified.

sources.title: SWE-Bench++: A Framework for the Scalable Generation of Software Engineering Benchmarks from Open-Source Repositories
sources.role: 11,133 instances from 3,971 repositories in 11 languages, built from live PRs.

sources.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
sources.role: Controlled experiment: Copilot group 55.8% faster on a JavaScript HTTP-server task.
cautions: One small, well-specified greenfield task; 35 completers per arm.

sources.title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
sources.role: User study (47 analysed): AI-assisted participants wrote less secure code yet rated it more secure.
cautions: Page range taken from the outline; DOI confirmed.

sources.title: Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot's Code Contributions
sources.role: Copilot output evaluated against MITRE Top-25 CWE scenarios.
cautions: Original IEEE S&P 2022 version reported about 40% of generated programs vulnerable; the CACM page read here gave no percentage, so the paper text does not quote one.

sources.title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
sources.role: Three field RCTs (Microsoft, Accenture, Fortune 100 firm), 4,867 developers: +26.08% completed tasks (SE 10.3%).
cautions: The publisher page did not list authors; author list from the SSRN/MIT working paper.

sources.title: SWE-bench experiments: open-sourced predictions, logs, trajectories and results of leaderboard submissions
sources.role: Primary data for this study's SWE-bench Verified re-analysis (per-instance results of 122 complete submissions).
cautions: 47 Verified entries have no results files and 13 report per-repo totals that are not the 500 Verified instances; both groups are excluded from the analysis but included in the product search.

sources.title: SWE-bench leaderboards (data/leaderboards.json)
sources.role: Leaderboard entries for all five SWE-bench boards, used to check for product-level submissions.
verified: searched all 5 boards for Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code and Codex
